key_findings: B outperforms C by ~3.5 quality points (small effect)
C outperforms A by ~8.5 quality points (large effect)
C is 67% more consistent (SD 8.3 vs 12.5) - fewer outliers
C loses 43% of actionability in synthesis (2.78 → 1.58)
C gains specificity (3.67 → 3.17 is -14%, but from same domain)
B has high variance (40-75 range) indicating inconsistency
C has narrow range (45-70) indicating robustness
Synthesis appears to be bottleneck in C (high specificity, moderate quality)

the_problem.title: Emergence Doesn't Beat Single-Agent Scaling
the_problem.description: 7 Haiku agents coordinated via SØWL synthesis do not produce better quality than 1 Sonnet agent with 8x token budget
the_problem.cause: Likely synthesis bottleneck - agents find specific insights but synthesis can't integrate them into actionable outputs
evidence: C specificity (3.17) is close to B (3.67) but actionability drops (1.58 vs 2.78)
Response length drops 76% (1,802 vs 7,757 chars) indicating information loss
C achieves 58.75 quality from 2.4K tokens; A achieves 50.33 from 1K tokens

what_it_means_if_b_stays_ahead.scenario: If d(B vs C) remains small-to-moderate positive at n=52
implications: Current 8OWLS architecture (parallel independence + serial synthesis) isn't optimal
Emergence requires architectural changes to manifest as quality advantage
however: C is more consistent (95% of C scores in 42-76 range)
C might be better for reliability-critical domains
The comparison is quality-per-token; emergence might optimize for other metrics
B has failure modes (sometimes scores 40); C rarely goes below 45
what_it_means_if_b_stays_ahead.not_a_failure: This is data clarifying which architecture works for what goal

what_emergence_could_win_on: Team collaboration (humans prefer seeing diverse expert input)
Certain domains (finance, medicine where redundancy matters)
If architecture changes (iterative agents, real specialization)

quick_wins: Give SØWL more tokens for synthesis (e.g., 4K instead of inherited)
Multi-level synthesis (pairs first, then combine results)
Explicit integration prompt for SØWL: 'Here are 7 perspectives, create action plan'
medium_term: Iterative agents (agents read each other, refine in rounds)
Specialized agent training (PERCEIVE expert ≠ LEARN expert)
Agent awareness (agents know what others focus on)
architectural_pivot: Show 7 perspectives to user, let them choose framework
Hybrid: Use C for reliability check, B for primary answer
Domain-specific routing (C for low-risk, B for high-reward)

diagnostic_tests_recommended.will_answer: If A+2.4K matches C, then emergence isn't providing unique value

diagnostic_tests_recommended.name: Iterative C with agent awareness
diagnostic_tests_recommended.will_answer: Whether synthesis bottleneck is the actual problem

immediate: Run diagnostic tests in parallel (A at 2.4K, iterative C)
Log failure modes (B low scores, C actionability gaps)
if_B_stays_ahead: Implement quick fix (SØWL gets more synthesis tokens)
if_convergence: Frame as portfolio: B for breakthrough, C for reliability
if_C_catches_up: Understand why emergence manifested with more data

statistical_caveats: B has smallest n (9) and highest variance (12.53) - most uncertain
Effect size d(B vs C) = 0.337 is small and could reverse with data
Confidence intervals overlap - cannot rule out B = C
Need at least n=30 per group for stable estimates
Small sample sizes mean sampling variation is high

quest_assessment.is_8OWLS_dead: No. But it's being tested and refined.
quest_assessment.quality_hypothesis: Emergence might not optimize for quality; it might optimize for reliability or diversity
quest_assessment.next_question: What do users actually need: brilliance or robustness?
quest_assessment.data_interpretation: Not a failure, a clarification. The data tells us which architecture works for which goal.
quest_assessment.recommendation: Continue experiment, run diagnostics, test hypotheses. Don't wait for n=52 to strategize.
